_comment: Generated Towers-side waves (waves.py; DESIGN.md section 12). Levels without a monster record play these.
threat: how hard each monster is to stop, per monster, before the wave's hp multiplier. It sizes waves
instead of draft cost, so prices can change without moving difficulty. Started from the 'fair cost'
column of analytics/matchups.py at the mid checkpoint.
budget: a generated wave's threat is challenge x (base + per_wave x d), d counting waves from the start of
the pass (level 1 wave 1 is 0). The last wave's elite or boss comes on top.
pack_pause: seconds between two packs of a wave (instead of the next monster's gap).
start: the roster before level 1 (looters are on it, but no pattern uses them: they only come as the hoard
counter). levels[i].new: the monsters a level brings in; they stay for the rest of the pass.
levels[i].waves, when given, scripts every wave instead (tuned by playtests, not the budget): a wave is a
list of packs, a pack a list of [kind, count] spawned in order. Levels past the list use the last entry,
with nothing new. levels[i].elite: the elite (monsters.json) that ends the level's last wave when no boss
does; the Champion when not given.
roles: what each wave of a level is for, as slots, each a share of the wave's threat: 'new' (the level's
newcomers, at least one of each), 'pattern' (a pattern from the roster) or 'stream' (the stream pattern).
A slot that overshoots its share takes it from the slots after it.
patterns: packs the generator draws from, used only when every kind in them is on the roster.
counters: what the scouts send against the towers on the map at the end of the last wave (waves.scout).
A tag is on top when its towers dealt main_tag_from of the last wave's damage (of the gold, if none); then share[level] x role_weight[role] of
the wave (plus escalation for every wave in a row the same tag stayed on top, up to escalation_max) goes
to the roster monsters that tag's towers find hardest: its scores, at least min_score, the `options` best.
They take the place of monsters from the back of the wave (single ones from streams and scripted packs,
then a pattern's whole repeats; never a newcomer or a monster that counters the tag already), so the
wave's threat doesn't change. (Weighing every tag by its share of the gold diluted the counters into
monsters mixed builds handle well: DESIGN.md section 12.)
scores: how hard each monster is for a tag's towers compared with the tag's other matchups, from
`uv run analytics/matchups.py --counter-scores` (rerun it after changing towers or monsters).
cluster: towers stacked within radius of one point of the path draw saboteurs (count[0] for exactly
'towers' of them, count[1] for more). hoard: banked gold of 'ratio' x the towers' value draws one looter
per ratio, up to 'max', hidden in the middle of the wave's heaviest pack. Both come from level 3 on,
with any counter share, and only once their monster is on the roster.
